messages.subject: shift model over theta continuum
parts:
Hi Phil,

i was under the impression that when i modify the group pars i could shift the model over the continuum, e.g. to have a model with mean = 50 and sd = 10, but this seems to be not true:

library(mirt)

model_1 = mirt(Science,1)
pars = mirt(Science, 1, pars = "values")
pars[pars$item == "GROUP","value"] = c(50,100)

model_2 = mirt(Science, 1, pars = pars)

itemplot(model_1, 1)
itemplot(model_2, 1)

hist(fscores(model_1)[,"F1"])
hist(fscores(model_2)[,"F1"])


i would have expected that slopes between model_1 and model_2 would be the same and the threshold parameters would be just shifted, but i guess, the group pars only go into fscore estimation? Is that true? is it possible to estimate a model with N(50,10)?

Best wishes, Felix

On Tue, Mar 3, 2015 at 1:59 PM, Dr. Hans Hansen <bea...@gmx.de> wrote:
Hi Phil,

i was under the impression that when i modify the group pars i could shift the model over the continuum, e.g. to have a model with mean = 50 and sd = 10, but this seems to be not true:

library(mirt)

model_1 = mirt(Science,1)
pars = mirt(Science, 1, pars = "values")
pars[pars$item == "GROUP","value"] = c(50,100)

model_2 = mirt(Science, 1, pars = pars)

itemplot(model_1, 1)
itemplot(model_2, 1)

hist(fscores(model_1)[,"F1"])
hist(fscores(model_2)[,"F1"])


i would have expected that slopes between model_1 and model_2 would be the same and the threshold parameters would be just shifted, but i guess, the group pars only go into fscore estimation? Is that true? is it possible to estimate a model with N(50,10)?

It's possible, but I highly don't recommend it. Basically, you're supplying a central density location that is very far from the integration grid, so every value in the grid essentially gets a very small likelihood (and therefore numerical issues arise, and the individual likelihood equations are not well computed). That's why the first model has a much higher log-likelihood than the first. Transforming scores this way is something I would advise against, so you'd be better to just apply a linear transformation on the typical scores after they are computed (e.g., X = theta * 10 + 50). Cheers.

Phil
 

Best wishes, Felix

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: shift model over theta continuum
parts:
You can of course, by changing the integration grid to be more suitable with the location parameters, but you really are inducing some numerical instabilities here. Specifying your own integration grid to get around this is possible, but I really do insist this is ad-hoc and harder to control (and not native to all functions yet). Nevertheless, if you want to experiment, here's how you can deal with the shifted locations.

Theta <- matrix(seq(0, 100, length=200))
model_3 = mirt(Science, 1, pars = pars, technical = list(customTheta=Theta))
coef(model_3)

For fscores(), I'll have to add an input to customize the integration grid as well to fix this. Will add that to the TODO list. Cheers.

Phil
